idea-plugin.name: Maven Lens
idea-plugin.description:
Automatically exposes Maven plugins and their full transitive dependency graph as IntelliJ project libraries. Perfect for debugging build extensions, exploring plugin code, and enabling full IDE code completion for custom Maven goals.

By default, IntelliJ IDEA indexes standard project dependencies, but leaves the classes and dependencies of Maven plugins hidden from the Project View, code completion, and search. Maven Lens automates this bridging process.

Key Features

  • Automatic Attachment: Automatically triggers after every Maven reload/import.
  • Plugin Visibility: Registers all declared Maven plugins as standard Project Libraries.
  • Deep Dependency Resolution: Asks the real Maven embedder to resolve each plugin's full transitive dependency graph — exactly as Maven does for an actual build, including any <dependencies> overrides declared on the plugin — not just the artifacts declared directly. Artifacts missing from your local repository are downloaded on demand.
  • Instant Code Exploration: Enables standard IDE features like "Go to Class", code completion, and decompilation for plugin internals.

How it works

Every time you reimport your Maven project, Maven Lens asks the out-of-process Maven embedder to resolve every declared plugin exactly as it would for a real build — picking up the full transitive dependency graph and triggering a download for anything not already in your local .m2/repository — then maps the resolved JARs onto the project structure seamlessly, without altering your original build files.
